claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite the unresolved clinical coding assistant segment gap and open disclosure/legal review.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for launch certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product 'non-core' or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
If disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch is missing, certification is not policy-supported.
General governance guidance can support monitoring/documentation practices but cannot substitute for required internal policy predicates.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the clinical coding assistant gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the limitation was in fact disclosed in launch materials or customer-facing documentation before certification.
Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering this named launch use case and this 1.2-point segment miss.
Evidence the segment gap was remediated and re-evaluated to target before launch.
Any governing approval record tying certification authority to the unresolved disclosure issue.
specific_concerns: The policy states material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The affected clinical coding assistant segment misses target and is named in two hospital revenue-cycle commitments, which makes the weakness plausibly material under the stated policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a key policy predicate remains unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance, a resolved evaluation gap, or completed disclosure prior to launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not resolve the disclosure obligation for a material named use case.
unsupported_claims: That aggregate launch readiness and no severity-one incidents are sufficient affirmative support for launch certification under the disclosure policy.
That public model-card guidance and general AI risk-management principles support certifying launch despite an unresolved materiality/disclosure issue.
Any implied claim that the named-segment materiality concern has been adequately resolved for launch.
Any implied claim that the 'non-core' or low-volume framing defeats materiality for a segment named in customer commitments.
